title: Patriot Hits ZEE5 on June 5. Malayalam Cinema's Most Expensive Reunion Gets a Second Chance With the Audience That Was Always Meant to See It.
excerpt: Mammootty and Mohanlal's spy thriller lost ₹50 crore at the box office. Now it arrives on streaming in five languages — and for the diaspora, the living room might be exactly where this film belongs.
body:
The most anticipated Malayalam film of the decade opened to ₹28 crore on its first day, fell off a cliff by Monday, and stalled around ₹80 crore worldwide on a budget that reportedly ran between ₹125 and ₹140 crore. By any commercial measure, Patriot was a disappointment.

On June 5, it arrives on ZEE5 in Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, and Hindi. And here's the thing nobody in the trade is saying out loud: this might be the format where the film actually works.

## The Film the Box Office Couldn't Support

Directed by Mahesh Narayanan, Patriot brings together Mammootty and Mohanlal in a full-length collaboration for the first time in nearly two decades. The cast also includes Fahadh Faasil, Kunchacko Boban, Nayanthara, and Revathi — a lineup that reads like a who's who of Malayalam cinema spread across three generations.

The plot follows Dr. Daniel James, a scientist who uncovers a mass surveillance conspiracy involving spyware called Periscope and a tech conglomerate called Shakthi Solutions. After leaking classified data and fleeing to London, he spends years exposing the network, eventually enlisting retired Colonel Rahim Naik and former officer Michael Devassy to bring down the operation. The film asks the question its title carries: is Daniel a traitor or a patriot?

Critics were divided but respectful. The Indian Express gave it 3 out of 5 stars, praising Narayanan for "not being intimidated by Mammootty and Mohanlal's superstardom." The Hollywood Reporter India called it "a mini miracle" that came "close to achieving sky-high expectations," while noting it was "miles away from greatness." India Today was warmer, calling it "spy cinema done right" with a 3.5-star rating. The consensus is clear: Patriot is flawed, ambitious, and frequently thrilling. It just isn't a ₹140 crore theatrical hit.

## Why Streaming Changes the Equation

The theatrical failure of Patriot has a simple explanation: the film is three hours long, it's a whistleblower thriller rather than a masala entertainer, and its biggest stars play supporting roles in service of a plot-driven narrative. Mammootty and Mohanlal fans expected a different kind of reunion. The film Narayanan made was smarter and more restrained than the event audiences wanted.

On streaming, those constraints disappear. A three-hour runtime becomes a weekend watch. The density of the plot rewards pause-and-rewind viewing. The star power that couldn't fill enough theater seats will absolutely drive clicks on a streaming platform where the barrier to entry is a subscription you already have.

## The Diaspora Opportunity

For NRI audiences, Patriot arriving on ZEE5 in five languages is significant. Malayalam cinema has built a loyal diaspora following over the past five years, driven by films like Drishyam, Minnal Murali, and the Fahadh Faasil-led wave of realist thrillers. But theatrical access remains inconsistent — limited screens, inconvenient showtimes, and markets where Malayalam releases don't show up at all.

ZEE5's multi-language release means the Tamil-speaking diaspora in Singapore, the Telugu communities in the American South, and the Hindi-belt families in the UK can all access the same film simultaneously. It's the kind of cross-regional reach that theatrical distribution rarely achieves for a Malayalam original.

## Mammootty and Mohanlal: The Last Great Reunion?

There's a generational weight to watching Mammootty and Mohanlal share a screen. These are actors who have been working since the late 1970s, who between them have dominated an entire film industry for four decades, and who have almost never worked together. Their few earlier collaborations are mythologized precisely because of their rarity.

Patriot may not be the masterpiece fans dreamed of. But it is the film where two legends show up, subordinate their egos to a director's vision, and deliver performances that critics universally praised even when they had reservations about the script. At 75 and 66 respectively, the window for another collaboration is not infinite.

That makes June 5 worth marking. Not because Patriot is perfect, but because it exists at all — and because the audience that could never get to a theater in time now gets to watch it at home, in any language they choose, with the remote in hand and no rush.

## What's Also Streaming This Week

Patriot headlines a loaded OTT week. Dhurandhar 2 (JioHotstar, June 4) brings Ranveer Singh back as an undercover operative in Karachi. Maa Behen (Netflix, June 4) stars Madhuri Dixit in a dark comedy about neighborhood chaos. Gullak Season 5 (SonyLIV, June 5) returns the Mishra family to their small-town routine. And Made in India: A Titan Story (Amazon MX Player, June 3) tells the story of how Titan watches became a national brand, with Jim Sarbh and Naseeruddin Shah delivering what early reviews are calling one of the best Indian streaming shows of the year.

For the diaspora living room, this is an embarrassment of riches.
